body_paragraphs: I am writing about the deposit of £1,150.00 I paid for Flat 2, 10 Sample Road, which is protected with the Deposit Protection Service. My tenancy ended and I moved out on 31 August 2026. I wrote to you on 12 September asking for the evidence behind your proposed deductions and have not had a reply.
I accept the £25.00 deduction for the replacement oven shelf. I do not accept the other two deductions, set out in the table below.

Carpet cleaning (£180.00): I had the carpets professionally cleaned on 29 August 2026, before I left, and I have the receipt. I am happy to send a copy. Please send me any evidence you rely on to show further cleaning was needed.

Repainting the living room (£350.00): the marks are light scuffs after two years of ordinary living, which is fair wear and tear. A landlord can’t charge a tenant for normal wear from everyday use. The check-in inventory and my move-out photos show the walls were in a similar condition, allowing for two years of use.

Please return £1,125.00 within 14 days of the date of this letter, or tell me in writing that you have asked the Deposit Protection Service to release it. If you still wish to make the disputed deductions, please confirm this in writing so that the dispute can be referred to the scheme’s free dispute resolution service.
evidence_to_gather: Find the check-out report the agent made, if there was one, and ask the agent for a copy if you haven’t had it.
Gather your dated move-out photos of the living room walls and carpets.
Keep the carpet cleaning receipt from 29 August 2026.
Keep the agent’s email of 10 September and your reply of 12 September.
